content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge uses the absence of a statement in the cited texts—that neither states Joseph begat the child—as part of the basis for holding the defense.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"neither text states that Joseph begat the child ([L4])","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'single verse does not state a link or its contrary'—I weighed reading it as barring reliance on verse silence to support STANDS/UNDERDETERMINED against reading it as barring only a bare one-verse ground.","why":"The judge treats the texts' silence on Joseph begetting the child as supporting the holding, which K-S2 forbids when verse non-statement is used as a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED."}
